M01.reason: The IDLE-to-SETUP transition fires when no request event exists and not when one arrives, so completer transfers are lost or spurious.

M02.reason: o_apb_pwakeup is 1 while i_rst_n_slv is low, even in APB4, which breaks the reset value of 0 and the 'APB5 outputs are 0' rule.

M03.reason: The change detector of the synchronizer model is inverted, so real input changes are not passed on and the crossing is corrupted.

M04.reason: With pend cleared on a delayed change, the pending value is never applied to sim_cur, so the crossing signal is lost and the handshake hangs.

M05.reason: With APB5=1 the requester wake-up is forced to 0 and never reaches o_apb_pwakeup while idle, so the synchronized-wake-up term is lost.

M06.reason: The model leaves reset with pend=1 and an undefined sim_nxt, so sim_cur takes X (or a stale value) after reset and the synchronized bit is corrupted.

M07.reason: The pending-delay countdown is inverted, so an extra delay of 1 becomes 2 cycles and 2 becomes 1. The timing differs for a given seed at the ports but stays inside the legal [N+1,N+3] window, which is why it survives.

M08.reason: The reset branch of the mst control flops is inverted, so request, PREADY and wakeup are held at 0 during normal operation and run free while i_rst_n_mst is low.

M09.reason: The APB5 gate is inverted, so in APB4 o_apb_pwakeup follows the wake-up and in-progress terms instead of staying 0, and in APB5 it stays 0.

M10.reason: In the two-phase handshake the acknowledge is set to 1 instead of toggling, so the second transfer is never acknowledged.

M11.reason: The 2-FF cell resets to 1 instead of 0, so the synchronized request or acknowledge reads 1 after reset and creates a spurious event.

M12.reason: The reset condition of the cell is inverted, so the chain is held at 0 in normal operation and does not reset when RN is low.

M13.reason: In four-phase the acknowledge is never raised at the end of the transfer, so the requester never sees it and PREADY never comes.

M14.reason: In four-phase the request bit is never raised at the launch, so no completer transfer starts and the requester waits forever.

M15.reason: In run apb4.s1 no +APBCDC_MSYNC_EN plusarg is given, so $value$plusargs fails and this assignment never executes. sim_en stays at its default of 1 and the ports behave identically.

M16.reason: PSLVERR is set to 1 in the RESP state instead of being cleared, so o_apb_pslverr stays high after the PREADY cycle.

M17.reason: For two-phase the acknowledge event uses the level instead of comparing with the request bit, so the response is accepted at the wrong time or never.

M18.reason: The Access phase ends when i_apb_pready is low, not high, so wait states end the transfer and the completing edge does not.

M19.reason: In four-phase the acknowledge is not cleared after the request falls, so it stays high and the handshake never closes.

M20.reason: The pending-delay countdown is inverted, so an extra delay of 1 becomes 2 cycles and 2 becomes 1. The timing differs for a given seed at the ports but stays inside the legal window, which is why it survives.

M21.reason: The default of the model enable is 0, so the model is off with no plusarg and the output is the plain chain output. The random extra latency disappears and the crossing latency is always nominal; this is still legal, which is why it survives.

M22.reason: After an immediate (extra 0) update, pend stays 1 with a stale or undefined sim_nxt, so the next edge overwrites sim_cur with a wrong value.

M23.reason: The zero-delay test is inverted: extra=0 starts a pending countdown with cnt=-1 that never completes, so the change is lost.

M24.reason: The launch condition is inverted, so the request and payload are launched when no Setup exists, and a real Setup does not launch.

M25.reason: The 'transfer in progress' term is true only in IDLE, so in APB5 o_apb_pwakeup is low during Setup and Access and high when idle.

M26.reason: PSEL is also high for the IDLE and other next states (any state except ACCESS), so o_apb_psel is high outside a transfer.

M27.reason: In apb4.s1 PARA_APBCDC_APB5=0. reg_wakeup is only reset to 1 during reset and is 0 after the first clock. Its only sink is o_apb_pwakeup, which the slv block gates with APB5!=0, so no output can change.

M28.reason: The four-phase request clear is decoded in every state except WAIT, so the request is not cleared when the acknowledge is seen and the handshake never closes.

M29.reason: The response hold register loads when the transfer is not done, so PRDATA, PSLVERR and the user response are not the values sampled at the completion edge.

M30.reason: The acknowledge resets to 1 against a request of 0, so after reset the slv sees a spurious request event and starts a transfer that never occurred.

M31.reason: The reset branch of the model is inverted, so it is held in reset during normal operation and the crossing is blocked.

M32.reason: The line clears pend after a delayed change is applied. Leaving it at 1 is harmless: pend is only stuck after the apply, when cnt is 0 and sim_nxt equals sim_cur. The extra updates rewrite the same value, and any new input change takes priority and overwrites pend, so the output never changes.

M33.reason: The reset condition of the mst FSM is inverted, so the FSM is held in IDLE in normal operation and does not reset when i_rst_n_mst is low.

M34.reason: The two-phase request event is inverted (equal instead of different), so a transfer starts when there is no request and not when there is one.

M35.reason: The handshake-type test is inverted, so two-phase uses the four-phase level event and the request toggle is not recognised.

M36.reason: The request bit resets to 1 against an acknowledge of 0, so after reset the slv sees a spurious request and starts a transfer with no Setup.
